SearchAliases: does a dog have buddha nature
Senses.Explanation: Buddha-nature is an inherited category that the Chan record turns into a contested public claim rather than leaving as a settled possession. Named speakers say that all sentient beings have it and that none have it; Hongren denies it to a southerner, while Huineng answers that it does not follow north and south. Secretary Zhu asks where it is when both halves of a cut earthworm move, and an unnamed participant asks Nagarjuna about its size. Baizhang Huaihai describes a failure to see it, while Dahui Zonggao raises Yongjia Xuanjue's verse containing it. The same headword is affirmed, denied, located, questioned, missed, and raised for later scrutiny; this entry records that range without supplying a metaphysical substance behind the word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 溈山示眾云：「一切眾生皆無佛性。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yangshan Huiji of Yuanzhou (袁州仰山慧寂禪師語錄). The embedded attribution names Guishan Lingyou as the exact speaker who says that all sentient beings lack buddha-nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鹽官示眾云：「一切眾生皆有佛性。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yangshan Huiji of Yuanzhou (袁州仰山慧寂禪師語錄). The embedded attribution names Yanguan Qi'an as the exact speaker who says that all sentient beings have buddha-nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「汝嶺南人，無佛性也。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Hongren section. Hongren is the exact speaker who tells the visiting southerner that he has no buddha-nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 行者云：「人則有南北，佛性無南北。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Hongren section. Huineng, still called the postulant, is the exact speaker who answers that people have north and south but buddha-nature does not.

Occurrences.Kwic: 竺尚書問：蚯蚓斬為兩段，兩頭俱動，未審佛性在阿那頭？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要), Changsha Jingcen section. The source names Secretary Zhu as the exact non-master questioner asking where buddha-nature is in the divided earthworm; Changsha Jingcen answers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸菩薩觀如地獄苦沉空滯寂不見佛性
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Baizhang Huaihai record. Baizhang Huaihai is the exact speaker who describes remaining sunk in emptiness and stuck in stillness as not seeing buddha-nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂舉永嘉云。江月照松風吹。永夜清宵何所為。佛性戒珠心地印。霧露雲霞體上衣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui Zonggao explicitly raises a verse by Yongjia Xuanjue. Under the quoted-speech rule, Yongjia is the historical utterer of the headword-bearing verse, while Dahui is the current reciter and later raiser.
